correctness.summary: Braun-Li's uniform lower and upper Fermi-coordinate time-separation estimates apply directly to matched transverse probability laws. The identity transverse coupling gives the lower bound, while the upper estimate holds for arbitrary endpoint pairs and its second-order curvature term depends only on the first marginal. Integration therefore yields the raw second-moment contraction tr(A_v M_mu). Rank-one and polarization reconstructions are algebraic consequences, and timelike sectional measurements separate algebraic curvature tensors by polynomial continuation and curvature polarization.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Braun-Li reconstruct timelike Ricci curvature from isotropic codimension-one slice measures, while Barton-Borza-Roehrig reconstruct timelike Ricci curvature from symmetric causal-diamond measures. Their proofs expose an unaveraged curvature quadratic form, but targeted literature and SCOPE searches did not locate the arbitrary matched-law second-moment formula, rank-one Lorentz-Wasserstein sectional-curvature recovery, finite tidal-operator tomography, or finite full-Riemann-tensor tomography stated here.

value.summary: The result upgrades a new Ricci-reconstruction observable into a directional curvature sensor. Explicit two-point probes recover the complete timelike tidal operator with n(n+1)/2 scalar limits, and varying the timelike direction yields algebraic identifiability of the full Riemann tensor with a linearly minimal basis-sized family of scalar measurements.

limitations: The theorem is local and asymptotic and inherits the condition epsilon=o(delta^(5/2)).
No discrete causal-set anisotropic estimator or convergence theorem is proved.
Finite-scale bias, statistical noise, and reconstruction conditioning are not analyzed.
The full-curvature probe family is existential rather than an optimized canonical design.
Rank-one leading-order sectional curvature is classically related to second variation; the new content is the matched-law Lorentz-Wasserstein contraction and finite transport-tomography consequences.
The two closest Lorentzian Ollivier-Ricci papers are very recent, so unindexed or differently phrased parallel observations remain a meaningful originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
